metadata.source_note: Entries originally derived from the flashcard deck named in 'source'. All 128 entries were re-sourced on 2026-09-16 (see 'verification_log') and rewritten in original wording; no entry retains flashcard phrasing.
metadata.verification_caveat: Final state, 2026-09-16 close-out (recounted 2026-10-08): all 128 entries cite two or more approved sources, drawn from 65 distinct NIH/NCBI StatPearls articles (cited by NBK number in notes) plus Kenhub. 95 entries rest on two StatPearls articles - separately authored but one publisher; 33 span two publishers. No print reference (Gray's, Netter's, Moore's) has been consulted, and sources were read via machine summaries. teachmeanatomy.info is not an approved source and counts toward nothing. An earlier mid-session audit recorded 10/48/70 for two/one/none; that figure is superseded.
metadata.textbook_check_2026_10_09: All 128 entries checked 2026-10-09 against sources independent of StatPearls: the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (.edu, all 128 except the two serratus posterior muscles), the UW Musculoskeletal Atlas (.edu) for limb conflicts, Loyola LUMEN (.edu), Radiopaedia (.org) and Kenhub. Result: 116 agree, 9 documented source conflicts (mostly nerve root levels), 3 corrections (flexor digitorum superficialis insertion, transversus abdominis costal origin - reverting a 2026-09-16 change, psoas major origin). Every entry now rests on at least one non-StatPearls publisher. LIMITS: these are medical-school teaching tables and atlases, not the printed Gray's/Netter's/Moore's; pages were read through a summarising fetch tool, not verbatim.
metadata.head_muscles_2026_10_14: 43 head and anterior-neck muscles added 2026-10-14 (sections 12-16) at Jake's request ('everything in the head'). Each rests on the UAMS head-and-neck table (.edu) plus StatPearls (.gov), with Kenhub where StatPearls gave no attachments; sources cited per entry. Temporoparietalis omitted: no approved source for its attachments or nerve. Buccinator, levator labii superioris alaeque nasi, styloglossus and palatoglossus have no Z-Anatomy mesh. Conflicts left open in notes: procerus branch, occipitalis direction (StatPearls), depressor labii inferioris branch. Read via summarising fetch; no print reference.

muscles.name: PectoralisMinor
muscles.origin: Margins of the 3rd to 5th ribs, adjacent to their costochondral junctions.
muscles.insertion: Medial border and superior surface of the coracoid process of the scapula.
muscles.action: Stabilises the scapula by drawing it downward and anteriorly against the thoracic wall: depression, protraction and downward rotation. Assists inspiration when the scapula is fixed.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Medial pectoral nerve (C8-T1)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 to two approved sources: StatPearls NBK545241 (Pectoral Muscles, .gov) and Kenhub. NBK545241 lists both medial and lateral pectoral nerves; the medial is the conventional and consistent attribution and is recorded, with the lateral contribution noted here. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: SerratusAnterior
muscles.origin: Superolateral surfaces of the 1st to 8th ribs, sometimes reaching the 9th, on the lateral thoracic wall.
muscles.insertion: Anterior surface of the medial border of the scapula, from the superior to the inferior angle.
muscles.action: Draws the scapula forward around the thorax - protraction - and its inferior part rotates the scapula upward to allow elevation of the arm above the head. Holds the medial border against the thoracic wall; assists respiration when the shoulder girdle is fixed.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Long thoracic nerve (C5-C7)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 to two approved sources: StatPearls NBK531457 (Serratus Anterior Muscles, .gov) and Kenhub. NBK531457 adds that the superior part may take an independent branch from C4-C6 and the inferior part dual supply from the long thoracic and intercostal nerves. Long thoracic injury produces the winged scapula. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Subclavius
muscles.origin: Junction of the 1st rib and its costal cartilage, anterior to the costoclavicular ligament.
muscles.insertion: Subclavian groove on the inferior surface of the middle third of the clavicle.
muscles.action: Depresses the clavicle and anchors it at the sternoclavicular joint; assists elevation of the 1st rib.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Nerve to subclavius, also called the subclavian nerve (C5-C6)
muscles.notes: CORRECTION UPHELD FROM .gov, 2026-09-16: the original entry gave 'scapular depression and abduction'. StatPearls NBK545241 describes the muscle as depressing the shoulder and elevating the 1st rib, with no scapular attachment - it runs from the 1st rib to the clavicle. Confirmed against Kenhub. NBK545241 also names the costoclavicular ligament relationship, added to the origin. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09 against the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source): attachments and actions agree. SOURCE CONFLICT, documented not changed: TTUHSC gives the nerve to subclavius as C5 alone; C5-C6 retained (Kenhub, Moore's convention).

muscles.name: LevatorScapulae
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of C1-C4, from their posterior tubercles.
muscles.insertion: Medial border of the scapula, from the superior angle to the root of the scapular spine.
muscles.action: Scapular elevation, retraction and downward rotation of the glenoid cavity; stabilises the scapula during movement. Acting on the neck: unilateral lateral flexion toward the contracting side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Dorsal scapular nerve (C5), with direct branches from the anterior rami of C3-C4
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 to two approved sources: StatPearls NBK537216 (Back, Extrinsic Muscles, .gov) and Kenhub. Both give the dual supply - dorsal scapular plus direct C3-C4 branches - which is why a dorsal scapular nerve injury does not abolish its function. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Rhomboids(major&minor)
muscles.origin: Minor: lower ligamentum nuchae and the spinous processes of C7-T1 with their supraspinous ligaments. Major: spinous processes of T2-T5.
muscles.insertion: Minor: medial border of the scapula at the level of the scapular spine. Major: medial border between the scapular spine and the inferior angle.
muscles.action: Scapular retraction, drawing it medially and superiorly, with downward rotation of the glenoid cavity. Hold the medial border against the thoracic wall.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Dorsal scapular nerve (C4-C5)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 to two approved sources: StatPearls NBK537216 (.gov) and Kenhub. Root range widened from C5 to C4-C5 per NBK537216. The minor/major split of the origin, added earlier the same day, is confirmed. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09 against the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source): attachments and actions agree. SOURCE CONFLICT, documented not changed: TTUHSC gives the dorsal scapular nerve as C5 alone; C4-C5 retained.

muscles.name: Trapezius(upper)
muscles.origin: External occipital protuberance, medial third of the superior nuchal line, and the ligamentum nuchae, which itself attaches to the spinous processes of C1-C6.
muscles.insertion: Posterior border of the lateral third of the clavicle.
muscles.action: Scapular elevation, retraction (adduction), and upward rotation. Bilateral: extension of the head and neck. Unilateral: lateral flexion toward the contracting side with rotation of the face away.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Accessory nerve (CN XI) for motor supply, with proprioceptive fibres from C3-C4
muscles.notes: Verified 2026-09-16 against Kenhub and StatPearls (NBK518994). A suspected error was checked and found NOT to be one: the reference to C1-C6 spinous processes looked wrong because the atlas has no spinous process, but the attachment is by way of the ligamentum nuchae, which Kenhub describes the same way. The origin is now explicit about that path, and 'medial third' has been added to the superior nuchal line. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Trapezius(middle)
muscles.origin: Spinous processes and supraspinous ligaments of C6-T3.
muscles.insertion: Medial margin of the acromion and the superior crest of the scapular spine.
muscles.action: Scapular retraction, drawing it medially, with assistance in upward rotation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Accessory nerve (CN XI) for motor supply, with sensory and proprioceptive fibres from the ventral rami of C3-C4
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 to three approved sources: StatPearls NBK518994 (Back, Trapezius) and NBK537216 (Back, Extrinsic Muscles), both .gov, plus Kenhub. SOURCE VARIATION on the vertebral range, not resolved: both .gov articles describe the whole muscle as arising from C7-T12 without subdividing it, Kenhub gives T1-T4 for the transverse part, and kinesiology texts commonly give C7-T3. The existing C6-T3 sits within that spread and has been kept rather than picked over the alternatives. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Trapezius(lower)
muscles.origin: Spinous processes and supraspinous ligaments of T4-T12.
muscles.insertion: Aponeurosis at the medial end of the scapular spine, onto its tubercle.
muscles.action: Scapular depression, retraction (adduction), and upward rotation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Accessory nerve (CN XI) for motor supply, with proprioceptive fibres from C3-C4
muscles.notes: Verified 2026-09-16 against Kenhub and StatPearls (NBK518994); T4-T12 range confirmed exactly. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: PectoralisMajor(clavicularhead)
muscles.origin: Anterior surface of the medial half of the clavicle.
muscles.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular (bicipital) groove of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder flexion to approximately 90 degrees, horizontal adduction, and internal rotation. Assists adduction when the arm is abducted less than 90 degrees.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral pectoral nerve (C5-C7)
muscles.notes: REVISED 2026-09-16. The entry previously also claimed 'abduction when arm is abducted >90 degrees'. Neither Kenhub nor StatPearls (NBK545241) attributes any abduction to the clavicular head; it appears to be a kinesiology-text claim about assisting elevation past 90 degrees. Moved here rather than shown as fact - re-source before returning it to the action field. Origin, insertion and nerve confirmed by both sources. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: PectoralisMajor(sternalhead)
muscles.origin: Anterior surface of the sternum and the costal cartilages of the 1st-6th ribs; the lowest fibres arise from the aponeurosis of the external oblique.
muscles.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular (bicipital) groove of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder adduction, horizontal adduction, and internal rotation. Extends the flexed arm back toward the anatomical position.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Medial pectoral nerve (C8-T1)
muscles.notes: Verified 2026-09-16 against Kenhub and StatPearls (NBK545241); all four fields confirmed. The abdominal slip from the external oblique aponeurosis has been added - both sources describe it, the entry did not. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Deltoid(anteriorhead)
muscles.origin: Anterior surface of the lateral third of the clavicle.
muscles.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity on the lateral surface of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder flexion and internal rotation; horizontal adduction. Works with pectoralis major to flex the arm during walking.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Axillary nerve (C5-C6)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK537056 (Deltoid Muscle) and NBK546633 (Scapulohumeral Muscles). Both confirm origin, insertion and nerve. The abduction previously credited to this head is not supported by either: NBK537056 assigns abduction to the acromial fibres and describes the anterior fibres as flexors. Dropped from the action. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Deltoid(middlehead)
muscles.origin: Superolateral surface of the acromion of the scapula.
muscles.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity on the lateral surface of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder abduction, raising the arm from roughly 15 to 100 degrees. It cannot initiate abduction because it contracts parallel to the humeral axis; supraspinatus performs the first 15 degrees.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Axillary nerve (C5-C6)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against StatPearls NBK537056 and NBK546633, both .gov. Range corrected from 15-90 to 15-100 degrees, which both give. The reason it cannot initiate abduction - line of pull parallel to the humerus - is from NBK537056 and is worth keeping for a clinical audience. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Deltoid(posteriorhead)
muscles.origin: Inferior border of the spine of the scapula.
muscles.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity on the lateral surface of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder extension and external rotation; horizontal abduction. Works with latissimus dorsi to extend the arm during walking.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Axillary nerve (C5-C6)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against StatPearls NBK537056 and NBK546633, both .gov. Abduction dropped for the same reason as the anterior head - neither source assigns it to these fibres. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: LatissimusDorsi
muscles.origin: Lateral sides of the spinous processes of T7-T12, the thoracolumbar fascia, the posterior iliac crest, and the proximal third of the 9th-12th ribs.
muscles.insertion: Floor of the intertubercular (bicipital) groove of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder adduction, extension and internal rotation; horizontal abduction. Raises the trunk toward the arm when the humerus is fixed, as in climbing, and is active in forced expiration.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Thoracodorsal nerve (C6-C8)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 to two approved sources: StatPearls NBK537216 (Back, Extrinsic Muscles, .gov) and Kenhub. NBK537216 gives the rib range as 9-12 and adds the forced-expiration role. Its thoracodorsal supply from the posterior cord is why it is spared in most brachial plexus upper-trunk injuries. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source); the UW Musculoskeletal Atlas (rad.uw.edu, .edu). Root levels: TTUHSC gives C7-C8, the UW Musculoskeletal Atlas C6-C8; C6-C8 retained.

muscles.name: TeresMajor
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the inferior angle and lower third of the lateral border of the scapula.
muscles.insertion: Medial lip of the intertubercular (bicipital) groove of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder extension, adduction and internal rotation; assists in stabilising the humeral head.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lower subscapular nerve (C5-C7)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK580487 (Teres Major Muscle) and NBK546633. Root range corrected from C5-C6 to C5-C7 per NBK580487, which states the lower subscapular nerve arises from C5, C6 and C7. SOURCE CONFLICT, not resolved: NBK546633 lists both the thoracodorsal and lower subscapular nerves; NBK580487 names the lower subscapular alone, which is the conventional attribution and is what is recorded. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09 against the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source); the UW Musculoskeletal Atlas (rad.uw.edu, .edu): attachments and actions agree. SOURCE CONFLICT, documented not changed: Root levels differ between sources: TTUHSC gives the lower subscapular nerve as C5-C6, the UW Musculoskeletal Atlas as C6-C7; C5-C7 recorded as the span of both.

muscles.name: Coracobrachialis
muscles.origin: Apex of the coracoid process of the scapula, shared with the short head of biceps brachii.
muscles.insertion: Middle third of the medial surface of the humeral shaft.
muscles.action: Shoulder flexion and weak adduction.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5-C7)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK546633 and NBK554420 (Arm Muscles). All four fields confirmed. The musculocutaneous nerve pierces this muscle, which is why it is the landmark for the nerve in the axilla. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Supraspinatus (*rotator cuff muscle group)
muscles.origin: Supraspinous fossa of the scapula.
muscles.insertion: Superior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus.
muscles.action: Initiates shoulder abduction through the first 15 degrees, before the deltoid can act; stabilises the humeral head in the glenoid cavity.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Suprascapular nerve (C5-C6)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK441844 (Rotator Cuff) and NBK546633. C5-C6 confirmed by both, upholding the correction made earlier the same day from the previous 'C5'. SOURCE CONFLICT, not resolved: NBK546633 adds lateral rotation to the action; NBK441844 gives abduction alone, which is recorded. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Infraspinatus (*rotator cuff muscle group)
muscles.origin: Infraspinous fossa of the scapula.
muscles.insertion: Middle facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus, below the supraspinatus attachment.
muscles.action: External rotation of the humerus - the most powerful external rotator; stabilises the humeral head in the glenoid cavity.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Suprascapular nerve (C5-C6)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK441844 and NBK546633. The abduction and horizontal abduction in the original flashcard entry are supported by neither and have been dropped; NBK441844 calls it a powerful lateral rotator and nothing more. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: TeresMinor (*rotator cuff muscle group)
muscles.origin: Upper part of the posterior surface of the lateral border of the scapula, below the infraglenoid tubercle.
muscles.insertion: Inferior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus, below the infraspinatus tendon.
muscles.action: External rotation of the humerus; stabilises the glenohumeral joint as part of the rotator cuff.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Axillary nerve (C5-C6)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK441844 and NBK513324 (Teres Minor Muscle). The adduction and extension carried in the original entry are described by neither - NBK513324 was asked directly and states the muscle is not an adductor or extensor. Removed rather than kept as 'assists'. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Subscapularis (*rotator cuff muscle group)
muscles.origin: Medial two-thirds of the subscapular fossa on the anterior surface of the scapula.
muscles.insertion: Lesser tubercle of the humerus.
muscles.action: Internal rotation of the humerus; prevents anterior displacement of the humeral head during abduction. Assists adduction and extension from certain positions.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Upper and lower subscapular nerves (C5-C7)

muscles.name: OpponensDigitiMinimi
muscles.origin: Hook of the hamate and the adjacent flexor retinaculum.
muscles.insertion: Medial border of the 5th metacarpal.
muscles.action: Draws the 5th metacarpal forward and rotates it toward the thumb - flexion and supination of the metacarpal - deepening the hollow of the palm.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8-T1)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK537229 and NBK539810. The flexion-and-supination wording is NBK537229's. muscles.name: AdductorPollicis
muscles.origin: Oblique head: capitate and the bases of the 2nd and 3rd metacarpals. Transverse head: palmar surface of the shaft of the 3rd metacarpal.
muscles.insertion: Ulnar side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb and the extensor hood, over a sesamoid bone.
muscles.action: Adduction of the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint; assists flexion at the metacarpophalangeal joint.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8-T1)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK526059 (Hand Adductor Pollicis) and NBK537229. The extensor hood attachment is from NBK526059 and was absent from the entry. Its weakness produces Froment's sign - compensatory thumb IP flexion by flexor pollicis longus when pinching a sheet of paper. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Dorsal Interossei (Hand)
muscles.origin: Each by two heads from the adjacent sides of the shafts of two metacarpals: the 1st from metacarpals 1-2, the 2nd from 2-3, the 3rd from 3-4, the 4th from 4-5.

muscles.action: Abduction of the 2nd, 3rd and 4th fingers away from the axis of the hand, taken through the middle finger; assists flexion at the metacarpophalangeal joints and extension at the interphalangeal joints.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8-T1)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK534772 (Hand Interossei Muscles) and NBK537229. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Palmar Interossei (Hand)
muscles.origin: Palmar surfaces of the 2nd (ulnar side), 4th and 5th (radial side) metacarpals.

muscles.name: Lumbricals (Hand)
muscles.origin: Tendons of flexor digitorum profundus in the palm: the 1st and 2nd from the radial side of the tendons to the index and middle fingers, the 3rd and 4th by two heads from adjacent tendons.

muscles.action: Flexion at the metacarpophalangeal joints with simultaneous extension at the interphalangeal joints, by pulling on the extensor hood.

muscles.name: Sternocleidomastoid
muscles.origin: Sternal head: superior part of the anterior surface of the manubrium. Clavicular head: superior surface of the medial third of the clavicle.
muscles.insertion: Lateral surface of the mastoid process, continuing onto the lateral half of the superior nuchal line of the occipital bone.
muscles.action: Bilateral: flexes the lower cervical spine while extending the head at the atlanto-occipital joint; assists inspiration by raising the sternum and clavicle. Unilateral: lateral flexion toward the contracting side with rotation of the face to the opposite side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Accessory nerve (CN XI) for motor supply, with proprioceptive fibres from the cervical plexus (C2-C3)

All four fields confirmed. muscles.name: Scalenes(Anterior,Middle,Posterior)
muscles.origin: Anterior: anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C3-C6. Middle: lateral parts of the atlas and axis and the posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C3-C7. Posterior: posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C5-C7.
muscles.insertion: Anterior: scalene tubercle on the superior surface of the 1st rib, in front of the groove for the subclavian artery. muscles.action: Bilateral: cervical flexion; elevate the 1st and 2nd ribs in forced inspiration; contribute to postural stability of the neck. Unilateral: lateral flexion toward the contracting side with rotation to the opposite side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of the cervical spinal nerves (anterior C5-C6; middle C3-C8; posterior C6-C8)

NBK544222 adds the atlas and axis attachments of the middle scalene, which the entry lacked. Source variation on the posterior scalene's levels remains: C5-C7 here, against 'the last three or four cervical vertebrae' in NBK519058 and C4-C6 in the original entry. The gap between the anterior and middle scalenes is the interscalene triangle, through which the brachial plexus roots and subclavian artery pass. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09 against the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source): attachments and actions agree. Root-level spread, documented not changed.

muscles.origin: Spinous processes of T3-T6.
muscles.insertion: Transverse processes of the atlas and axis and the posterior tubercle of C3.
muscles.action: Bilateral: extension of the neck. Unilateral: lateral flexion and rotation toward the contracting side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral branches of the posterior (dorsal) rami of the lower cervical spinal nerves

muscles.name: SemispinalisCapitis
muscles.origin: Articular processes of C4-C6 and the transverse processes of C7-T7.
muscles.insertion: Medial half of the occipital bone between the superior and inferior nuchal lines.
muscles.action: Bilateral: extension of the head and neck. Unilateral: extension, lateral flexion, and weak rotation to the opposite side.

muscles.insertion: Major: occipital bone below the lateral part of the inferior nuchal line. Minor: occipital bone below the inferior nuchal line, medial to the major.
muscles.action: Major: head extension and rotation toward the contracting side, acting on the atlas as well as the head. Minor: weak head extension only.

muscles.insertion: Internal surface of the 12th rib and the transverse processes of L1-L4.

muscles.name: Transverse Abdominis
muscles.origin: Internal surfaces of the costal cartilages of the 7th-12th ribs (the lower six), thoracolumbar fascia, inner lip of the iliac crest, and the lateral third of the inguinal ligament.
muscles.insertion: Linea alba by the abdominal aponeurosis and rectus sheath, and the pubic crest by the conjoint tendon.
muscles.action: Compresses the abdominal contents and raises intra-abdominal pressure - abdominal hollowing. Contributes no significant trunk movement.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of T7-T11, T12 (subcostal), and the iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves (L1)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK551649 and NBK525975. Rib range for the costal origin adjusted from the 7th-12th to the 5th-10th costal cartilages per NBK551649. The L1 contribution is correct for this muscle. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09 - CORRECTED: Costal origin corrected 2026-10-09 BACK to the 7th-12th costal cartilages (the lower six ribs). The 2026-09-16 change to the 5th-10th followed NBK551649 alone and is not supported elsewhere: TTUHSC tables (.edu) give the lower 6 ribs and Kenhub gives the internal surfaces of costal cartilages 7-12, matching the classical description. Checked against the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source); Kenhub.

muscles.name: SerratusPosteriorSuperior
muscles.origin: Lower ligamentum nuchae and the spinous processes of C7-T3 with their supraspinous ligaments.
muscles.insertion: Posterosuperior surfaces of the 2nd-5th ribs, lateral to their angles.
muscles.action: Elevates the 2nd-5th ribs; accessory muscle of inspiration.
muscles.nerve_innervation: 2nd-5th intercostal nerves
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 to two approved sources: StatPearls NBK538321 (Thorax, Muscles, .gov) and Kenhub. Both confirm the rib range and the inspiratory role. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with Radiopaedia (.org).

muscles.name: SerratusPosteriorInferior
muscles.origin: Spinous processes of T11-L2 and their supraspinous ligaments.
muscles.insertion: Inferoposterior surfaces of the 9th-12th ribs, lateral to their angles.
muscles.action: Depresses the lower ribs; accessory muscle of expiration.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of T9-T11 and the subcostal nerve (T12)
muscles.notes: CORRECTION UPHELD FROM .gov, 2026-09-16: the original entry had this muscle depressing the ribs 'during inspiration'. StatPearls NBK538321 places it in forced EXPIRATION, as does Kenhub - two approved sources against the flashcard. The classical account, that it anchors the lower ribs against diaphragmatic pull during inspiration, is recorded here as the minority position rather than displayed as fact. SOURCE CONFLICT on the rib range, not resolved: NBK538321 gives ribs 8-12, Kenhub and the original entry give 9-12. The nerve field also read '9th-12th intercostal nerves'; there is no 12th intercostal nerve. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with Radiopaedia (.org).

muscles.name: ExternalIntercostals
muscles.origin: Inferior borders of the 1st-11th ribs, running from the rib tubercle posteriorly to the costochondral junction anteriorly.
muscles.insertion: Superior borders of the 2nd-12th ribs, the fibres running inferomedially.
muscles.action: Elevate the ribs during inspiration, increasing the transverse diameter of the thorax; resist indrawing of the intercostal spaces in quiet breathing.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Intercostal nerves, the anterior rami of T1-T11
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK538321 and NBK535414 (Thorax, Wall). Both give T1-T11 and the inspiratory role. NBK535414 adds that the anterior fibres are replaced by the external intercostal membrane, which is why the muscle does not reach the sternum. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with Loyola LUMEN Master Muscle List (lumen.luc.edu, .edu); the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: InternalIntercostals
muscles.origin: Costal groove of the 1st-11th ribs and the adjacent costal cartilages, running from the sternum anteriorly to the rib angles posteriorly.
muscles.insertion: Superior borders of the 2nd-12th ribs, the fibres running inferolaterally.
muscles.action: Depress the ribs during forced expiration; stabilise the ribs in quiet breathing.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Intercostal nerves, the anterior rami of T1-T11
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK538321 and NBK535414. Attachments given in the anatomical convention - costal groove of the rib above to the superior border of the rib below - which both sources use. NBK535414 adds that the posterior fibres are replaced by the internal intercostal membrane. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: LevatorCostarum
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of C7-T11.
muscles.insertion: External surface of the rib one level below, between the tubercle and the angle; the lower four also send a longer slip two levels down.
muscles.action: Elevate the ribs, contributing minimally to inspiration. Assist rotation and lateral flexion of the thoracic spine.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral branches of the posterior (dorsal) rami of C8-T11
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 to two approved sources: StatPearls NBK538321 (.gov) and Kenhub. Both give the C7-T11 origin and attachment to the rib below. NBK538321 describes the respiratory contribution as minimal, and Kenhub notes the role in quiet respiration is debated - recorded rather than resolved. SOURCE NOTE: NBK538321 attributes them to intercostal nerves, Kenhub to the posterior rami; the posterior-rami attribution is conventional for a muscle of the deep back and is recorded. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with Loyola LUMEN Master Muscle List (lumen.luc.edu, .edu); the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Diaphragm
muscles.origin: Sternal part: two slips from the posterior surface of the xiphoid process. Costal part: internal surfaces of the lower six costal cartilages and adjacent ribs. Lumbar part: right crus from the bodies of L1-L3, left crus from L1-L2, with the medial and lateral arcuate ligaments.
muscles.insertion: Central tendon of the diaphragm.
muscles.action: The principal muscle of inspiration: contraction pulls the central tendon inferiorly and flattens the dome, increasing the vertical dimension of the thoracic cavity. Raises intra-abdominal pressure during straining.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Phrenic nerve (C3-C5), with sensory supply to the periphery from the lower intercostal nerves
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK519558 (Thorax: Diaphragm) and NBK538321. Both confirm the three named parts and C3-C5; NBK519558 gives the asymmetric crura - right from L1-L3, left from L1-L2 - which the original entry lacked entirely. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source); Loyola LUMEN Master Muscle List (lumen.luc.edu, .edu).

muscles.name: TransverseThoracis
muscles.origin: Internal surface of the lower body of the sternum and the xiphoid process, and the sternal ends of the costal cartilages of the 4th-7th ribs.
muscles.insertion: Internal surfaces of the costal cartilages of the 2nd-6th ribs.
muscles.action: Draws the 2nd-6th costal cartilages toward the sternum, weakly depressing the ribs during forced expiration; supports the intercostal spaces.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Intercostal nerves (T2-T6)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 to two approved sources: StatPearls NBK538321 (.gov) and Kenhub. Both give the insertion as ribs 2-6; Kenhub gives the origin as the sternal ends of the 4th-7th costal cartilages, correcting the 7th-10th of the original entry, and the T2-T6 nerve range. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Iliacus
muscles.origin: Upper two-thirds of the iliac fossa, with slips from the ala of the sacrum and the anterior sacroiliac ligament.
muscles.insertion: Lesser trochanter of the femur, by the tendon shared with psoas major, and the adjacent shaft.
muscles.action: Hip flexion - a prime mover; stabilises the pelvis during hip flexion and assists trunk flexion when the limb is fixed. Anterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Femoral nerve (L2-L4)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK531508 (Iliopsoas Muscle) and NBK500008 (Femoral Muscles). Both give femoral L2-L4, upholding the earlier correction from L2-L3. NBK531508 makes the point the paired entries now carry: iliacus and psoas major have DIFFERENT nerve supplies despite sharing a tendon. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: PsoasMajor
muscles.origin: Lateral surfaces of the bodies of T12-L5 and the intervening intervertebral discs, and the transverse processes of all five lumbar vertebrae.
muscles.insertion: Lesser trochanter of the femur, by the tendon shared with iliacus.
muscles.action: Hip flexion - a prime mover; assists adduction and external rotation. Stabilises the lumbar spine in sitting; lumbar flexion and lateral flexion; anterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of L1-L3, directly from the lumbar plexus rather than through a named nerve
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK531508 and NBK500008. Both give L1-L3 direct from the lumbar plexus, in contrast to iliacus's femoral supply. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09 - CORRECTED: Origin extended 2026-10-09 from L1-L4 to T12-L5 (bodies) and all lumbar transverse processes: the UW Musculoskeletal Atlas gives transverse processes of L1-L5 and bodies and discs of T12-L5, and the UAMS/TTUHSC tables give the bodies and transverse processes of the lumbar vertebrae. Nerve: UW gives direct fibres of L1-L3 (as recorded); UAMS/TTUHSC give ventral rami L2-L4. Checked against the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source); the UW Musculoskeletal Atlas (rad.uw.edu, .edu).

muscles.name: PsoasMinor
muscles.origin: Body of the last thoracic vertebra, the first lumbar vertebra, and the intervening intervertebral disc.
muscles.insertion: Iliopectineal eminence and the iliac fascia.
muscles.action: Weak flexion of the lumbar spine. Acts on the vertebral column only - it has no femoral attachment and does not move the hip.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of L1-L2
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK535418 (Psoas Major) and NBK500008 (Femoral Muscles). NBK535418 puts its presence at 60-65 percent of people, so it is absent in roughly 35-40 percent, and notes it often degenerates into fibrous tissue - which is why this muscle has no mesh in the 3D model and the app reports that honestly. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Pectineus
muscles.origin: Pecten pubis on the superior ramus of the pubis.
muscles.insertion: Pectineal line on the posterior femur, from the lesser trochanter to the linea aspera.
muscles.action: Hip flexion and adduction; assists external rotation; anterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Femoral nerve (L2-L3), often with an additional branch from the obturator nerve
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK534775 (Medial Thigh Muscles) and NBK500008. Both give L2-L3 for pectineus specifically, even though the femoral nerve as a whole is L2-L4 - so unlike iliacus and sartorius, the original range was right here and has been kept. Worth noting as the case that broke the L2-L3 pattern found elsewhere in this section. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: RectusFemoris
muscles.origin: Straight head: anterior inferior iliac spine. Reflected head: groove above the acetabulum.
muscles.insertion: Base of the patella by the quadriceps tendon, and by the patellar ligament to the tibial tuberosity.
muscles.action: Knee extension and hip flexion - the only quadriceps component crossing both joints; anterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Femoral nerve (L2-L4)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK482445 (Thigh Muscles) and NBK500008. Both name the two heads and give femoral L2-L4. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Sartorius
muscles.origin: Anterior superior iliac spine and the area just below it.
muscles.insertion: Superomedial surface of the proximal tibia, as the most anterior of the three pes anserinus tendons.
muscles.action: Hip flexion, abduction and external rotation; knee flexion and internal rotation; anterior pelvic rotation and tilt. Produces the cross-legged sitting posture it is named for.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Femoral nerve (L2-L4)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK482445 and NBK500008, both giving femoral L2-L4 and upholding the earlier correction from L2-L3. The longest muscle in the body; shares the pes anserinus with gracilis and semitendinosus. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Gracilis
muscles.origin: Anterior body and inferior ramus of the pubis.
muscles.insertion: Medial surface of the proximal tibia at the pes anserinus, as the middle of its three tendons.
muscles.action: Hip adduction and flexion; knee flexion and internal rotation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Obturator nerve, anterior branch (L2-L4)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK534775 and NBK500008, both giving obturator anterior branch L2-L4 - upholding the earlier correction from L2-L3. The most superficial of the adductor group and the standard donor for free muscle transfer. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: TensorFasciaeLatae
muscles.origin: Anterior superior iliac spine and the outer lip of the anterior iliac crest.
muscles.insertion: Iliotibial tract, which continues to the lateral condyle of the tibia at Gerdy's tubercle.
muscles.action: Hip: internal rotation, abduction and flexion; stabilises the pelvis in standing and gait. Knee: external rotation of the leg, and stabilisation of the extended knee through the iliotibial tract.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 to two approved sources from different publishers: StatPearls NBK499870 (Tensor Fasciae Latae, .gov) and Kenhub. SOURCE CONFLICT on the knee, not resolved, and it partly vindicates the original entry: NBK499870 calls it an accessory knee FLEXOR once the knee is past about 30 degrees, while Kenhub says it can weakly flex OR EXTEND depending on the degree of knee flexion. Both agree on external rotation of the leg, which an earlier revision on 2026-09-16 had wrongly dropped as unsupported - it is restored. What both rule out is the flashcard's flat description of it as a knee extensor. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: AdductorBrevis
muscles.origin: Body of the pubis and the anteroinferior pubic ramus.
muscles.insertion: Upper third of the linea aspera and the posterior proximal femur.
muscles.action: Hip adduction and flexion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Obturator nerve, anterior branch (L2-L4)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK534775 and NBK500008. Both give adduction as the action; the extension-from-flexed and external rotation claims of the original flashcard entry are carried by neither and stay out. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: AdductorLongus
muscles.origin: Body of the pubis and the anteroinferior pubic ramus, just below the pubic crest.
muscles.insertion: Middle third of the linea aspera on the femoral shaft.
muscles.action: Hip adduction and flexion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Obturator nerve, anterior branch (L2-L4)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK534775 and NBK500008. The most commonly strained of the adductor group. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: AdductorMagnus
muscles.origin: Adductor (pubofemoral) part: inferior ramus of the pubis, ramus of the ischium, and the external obturator membrane. Hamstring (ischiocondylar) part: ischial tuberosity.
muscles.insertion: Adductor part: medial side of the gluteal tuberosity, the whole length of the linea aspera, and the medial supracondylar line. Hamstring part: adductor tubercle on the medial femoral condyle.
muscles.action: Adductor part: hip adduction, its superior segment also flexing the thigh. Hamstring part: hip adduction and extension.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Adductor part: obturator nerve, posterior branch (L2-L4). Hamstring part: tibial division of the sciatic nerve
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK534842 (Thigh Adductor Magnus) and NBK534775. Both confirm the two parts pull in opposite directions at the hip - the adductor part flexes, the hamstring part extends - which a single merged action line could not express. SOURCE CONFLICT on the hamstring part's root levels, not resolved: NBK534842 gives L4, NBK534775 gives L2-L4 for the muscle overall, other references give L4-S3; no single range is recorded as settled. NBK534842 also notes recent work suggesting the adductor part may receive dual obturator and tibial supply distally. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Gluteus Minimus
muscles.origin: Gluteal surface of the ilium, between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines.
muscles.insertion: Anterior aspect of the greater trochanter of the femur.
muscles.action: Hip abduction and internal rotation; assists flexion. With gluteus medius, stabilises the pelvis over the stance limb during gait.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 to two approved sources from different publishers: StatPearls NBK556144 (Gluteus Minimus, .gov) and Kenhub, with the nerve additionally confirmed by NBK535408. Both give the same attachments between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: GluteusMedius
muscles.origin: Gluteal surface of the ilium, between the anterior and posterior gluteal lines.
muscles.insertion: Lateral aspect of the greater trochanter of the femur, by fibrocartilage.
muscles.action: Hip abduction; anterior fibres internally rotate the thigh, posterior fibres externally rotate it with the knee extended. Holds the pelvis level over the stance limb - its failure produces the Trendelenburg sign, in which the pelvis sinks on the UNSUPPORTED side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 to two approved sources from different publishers: StatPearls NBK557509 (Gluteus Medius, .gov) and Kenhub, with the nerve additionally confirmed by NBK535408 (Superior Gluteal Nerve). NBK557509 specifies that the posterior fibres rotate laterally only with the knee extended, and that the Trendelenburg drop occurs on the unsupported side - commonly stated backwards. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: GluteusMaximus
muscles.origin: Gluteal surface of the ilium behind the posterior gluteal line, lateroposterior surface of the sacrum and coccyx, sacrotuberous ligament, and the thoracolumbar fascia.
muscles.insertion: Superficial fibres into the iliotibial tract; the deep quarter into the gluteal tuberosity of the femur, between adductor magnus and vastus lateralis.
muscles.action: Hip extension and external rotation. An antigravity muscle recruited in rising from sitting, stair climbing and running rather than level walking; extends the trunk from a flexed position and stabilises the pelvis in upright posture. Upper fibres abduct, lower fibres adduct.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Inferior gluteal nerve (L5-S2) - the only muscle this nerve supplies
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 to two approved sources from different publishers: StatPearls NBK538193 (Gluteus Maximus, .gov) and Kenhub. Both give the sacrotuberous ligament and thoracolumbar fascia in the origin and the split of superficial fibres to the iliotibial tract from deep fibres to the gluteal tuberosity - neither of which was in the original entry. Actions corroborated by NBK470555 (Hip Joint). TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Semitendinosus
muscles.origin: Inferomedial impression of the ischial tuberosity, by a tendon shared with the long head of biceps femoris.
muscles.insertion: Anteromedial surface of the proximal tibia below the medial condyle, as the most posterior of the three pes anserinus tendons.
muscles.action: Hip extension; knee flexion and internal rotation of the flexed knee; posterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve (L5-S2)
muscles.notes: Verified 2026-09-16 against StatPearls (NBK542215) and Kenhub. The shared conjoint tendon with biceps femoris long head has been made explicit, since it is what distinguishes both from semimembranosus. Source variation on the conjoint footprint, not resolved: classically the inferomedial impression, given as the superior medial quadrant by StatPearls. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: Semimembranosus
muscles.origin: Superolateral impression of the ischial tuberosity, separate from and deep to the conjoint tendon of semitendinosus and biceps femoris.
muscles.insertion: Posteromedial surface of the medial tibial condyle, with expansions into the oblique popliteal ligament and the popliteal fascia.
muscles.action: Hip extension; knee flexion and internal rotation of the flexed knee; posterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve (L5-S2)
muscles.notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-16: the origin previously read 'inferolateral surface of the ischial tuberosity'. Semimembranosus arises from the SUPEROLATERAL impression - confirmed by Kenhub and StatPearls (NBK542215), which gives 'superior lateral aspect'. It is the one hamstring not part of the conjoint tendon, and the entry as written placed it in the wrong quadrant of the tuberosity, which is exactly the landmark used to tell a proximal hamstring avulsion apart on imaging. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: BicepsFemoris
muscles.origin: Long head: ischial tuberosity, by the conjoint tendon shared with semitendinosus. Short head: lateral lip of the linea aspera and the proximal lateral supracondylar ridge of the femur.
muscles.insertion: Head of the fibula, with slips to the lateral tibial condyle and the fibular collateral ligament.
muscles.action: Long head: hip extension and external rotation. Both heads: knee flexion and external rotation of the flexed knee; posterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Long head: tibial division of the sciatic nerve (L5-S2). Short head: common fibular (peroneal) division of the sciatic nerve (L5-S2)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK542215 (Posterior Thigh Muscles) and NBK546688 (Hamstring Muscle). Both confirm the split innervation, which is why the short head can be spared in a sciatic injury affecting the tibial division. NBK546688 describes the proximal aponeurosis shared with semitendinosus extending about 7 cm from the ischial tuberosity. The short head is the only hamstring component not crossing the hip. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: VastusLateralis
muscles.origin: Intertrochanteric line, greater trochanter, gluteal tuberosity, and the lateral lip of the linea aspera.
muscles.insertion: Lateral border of the patella by the quadriceps tendon, and by the patellar ligament to the tibial tuberosity.
muscles.action: Knee extension; its oblique distal fibres draw the patella laterally, opposed by vastus medialis.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Femoral nerve (L2-L4)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK482445 (Thigh Muscles) and NBK500008 (Femoral Muscles). The largest of the four quadriceps components. TEXTBOOK-LEVEL CHECK 2026-10-09: agrees with the UAMS/TTUHSC medical-school anatomy tables (medicine.uams.edu, anatomy.ttuhscep.edu - .edu; identical tables from one lineage, counted as one source).

muscles.name: VastusIntermedius
muscles.origin: Anterolateral surface of the upper two-thirds of the femoral shaft.
muscles.insertion: Deep surface of the quadriceps tendon at the proximal border of the patella, and by the patellar ligament to the tibial tuberosity.
muscles.action: Knee extension.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Femoral nerve (L2-L4)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK482445 and NBK500008. Its deepest fibres form articularis genu, which retracts the suprapatellar bursa during extension. muscles.name: VastusMedialis
muscles.origin: Intertrochanteric line, medial lip of the linea aspera, medial supracondylar line, and the tendon of adductor magnus.

muscles.origin: Lateral femoral condyle and the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.
muscles.insertion: Posterior surface of the proximal tibia, above the soleal line.
muscles.action: Unlocks the fully extended knee to begin flexion, by internally rotating the tibia on the femur with the foot free, or externally rotating the femur on the tibia with the foot planted. Assists knee flexion and draws the lateral meniscus posteriorly during flexion.

muscles.origin: Medial head: posterior, non-articular surface of the medial femoral condyle. Lateral head: lateral surface of the lateral femoral condyle.

muscles.origin: Lower two-thirds of the lateral surface of the fibula and the anterior intermuscular septum.

muscles.origin: Lateral condyle of the tibia, the anterior surface of the fibula, and the adjacent interosseous membrane.

muscles.origin: Middle half of the anterior surface of the fibula and the adjacent interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Dorsal central aspect of the base of the distal phalanx of the great toe.

muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep fibular (peroneal) nerve (L4-S1)

muscles.action: The strongest dorsiflexor of the ankle, essential during the swing phase of gait; a primary inverter of the foot, working with tibialis posterior to supinate the medial arch.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep fibular (peroneal) nerve (L4-S1)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK513304 (Tibialis Anterior) and NBK539725 (Leg Anterior Compartment). muscles.name: TibialisPosterior
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the interosseous membrane, the proximal two-thirds of the posterior and medial surfaces of the fibula, and the superior posterior tibia.
muscles.insertion: Tuberosity of the navicular and plantar aspect of the medial cuneiform; a plantar slip to the bases of the 2nd-4th metatarsals, the intermediate and lateral cuneiforms and the cuboid; and a recurrent slip to the sustentaculum tali.
muscles.action: Foot inversion - the principal inverter - and ankle plantarflexion. Dynamically supports the medial longitudinal arch.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial nerve (L4-S3)

muscles.name: FlexorDigitorumLongus
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the middle third of the tibia, below the soleal line.
muscles.insertion: Plantar surfaces of the bases of the distal phalanges of the lateral four toes.

muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial nerve (L5-S2)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK537340 (Leg Posterior Compartment) and NBK546698. muscles.name: Flexor Hallucis Longus
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the distal two-thirds of the fibula and the adjacent interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Plantar surface of the base of the distal phalanx of the great toe.

muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial nerve (L5-S2)
muscles.notes: Re-sourced 2026-09-16 against two .gov sources: StatPearls NBK537340 and NBK546698. muscles.name: FlexorDigitorumBrevis
muscles.origin: Calcaneal tuberosity, plantar aponeurosis and the intermuscular septa.
muscles.insertion: Sides of the middle phalanges of the lateral four toes, each tendon splitting to let the flexor digitorum longus tendon pass through.

muscles.name: Abductor Digiti Minimi

muscles.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th toe.

muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral plantar nerve (S1-S3)

muscles.origin: Plantar surfaces of the cuboid and the lateral cuneiform, with a slip from the tendon of tibialis posterior.

muscles.origin: Calcaneal tuberosity, flexor retinaculum and plantar aponeurosis.

muscles.origin: Base of the 5th metatarsal and the adjacent plantar aponeurosis.
muscles.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th toe.

muscles.name: Piriformis
muscles.origin: Anterior surface of the sacrum, the gluteal surface of the ilium near the margin of the greater sciatic notch, the capsule of the sacroiliac joint, and sometimes the sacrotuberous ligament.
